title: Immutable Terraform module for Private EKS control plane with signal-driven upgrades and live health probes
creator: Maya Gupta
description:
Background: Customers running Redwood Private in VPCs require a predictable, auditable control-plane provisioning pipeline that supports safe, fast upgrades with minimal blast radius. Current terraform modules can mutate state in place and rely on manual sequences for upgrades; this ticket aims to deliver an immutable-first Terraform module and orchestration pattern that uses signal-driven canaries and live health probes to automate safe control-plane upgrades for Private EKS deployments.

Scope: Deliver a new Terraform module and supporting orchestration artifacts that implement: immutable provisioning of control-plane resources (versioned stacks instead of in-place mutates where safe), signal-based canary rollout (observability signals determine promotion), built-in liveliness and readiness probes for control-plane critical paths (API server, etcd connectivity, IAM auth), upgrade guard rails (preflight validations, kill-switch, automatic rollback on regressions), and telemetry hooks (logs/metrics/trace links) to the Redwood Console.

Out-of-scope: worker node autoscaling strategies, platform-wide runtime model routing, and on-prem packaging. This ticket focuses on control-plane provisioning and the upgrade orchestration layer for Private EKS clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exists under modules/priv-eks-controlplane and uses immutable-stack naming conventions for critical resources
Canary upgrade flow implemented: create new versioned control-plane, route small fraction of control-plane traffic (control-plane health checks) to new stack, promote on green signals
Health probes cover API server latency/P95, API error rate, node bootstrap success, and KV store (etcd) health; probes publish to metrics with tags cluster_id and upgrade_id
Automated rollback triggers on any probe failing threshold (configurable): rollback completes within SLA and leaves previous control-plane healthy
KMS-wrapped Terraform state handling and IAM roles scoped for least privilege; SSM/SecretsManager patterns documented
E2E test harness (terraform + synthetic probes) that runs in CI and validates canary promotion/rollback on simulated failures
Design and rollout playbook documented (Confluence) with runbook links, emergency rollback CLI commands, and post-mortem template
implementation_notes:
Design notes: we favor immutable stacks for versioned control-plane components (API server endpoints, control-plane ELBs, autoscaling groups where applicable) and use DNS alias swap for promotion to minimize in-place diffs. For components that cannot be created immutably (e.g., managed nodegroups with provider limitations) we implement preflight smoke tests and a two-phase drain/replace.

Upgrade orchestration: small controller (lambda + stepfunction prototype) will orchestrate TF apply for new stack, run live probes, collect metrics (export to CloudWatch/Prometheus), and evaluate SLOs against thresholds. If passes, controller flips DNS alias and tears down old stack; if fails, controller triggers rollback and creates incident with telemetry links.

Health checks: lightweight synthetic clients run against control-plane API and record P95 latency, 5xx rate, and kube-apiserver readiness. We also add an etcd client probe for managed or self-hosted stores when accessible. Probes are configurable and output structured metrics that Console can ingest.

Security: terraform state will remain in KMS-encrypted S3 with strict bucket policies; module requires explicit IAM principals; we will add a security checklist for KMS key rotation and HSM integration as follow-up.

Trade-offs: immutable stacks increase transient resource costs during upgrades but reduce complex in-place migrations and decrease upgrade flakiness. We accept higher short-term capacity cost for predictable rollback safety.
tasks: Module scaffold: create modules/priv-eks-controlplane with inputs/outputs and examples
Implement immutable naming and versioning conventions
Add preflight validators that check current cluster state, nodegroup compatibility, and networking constraints
Build orchestration controller prototype (Step Function + Lambda) to run canary TF applies and probe evaluation
Implement probe suite: api_latency, api_errors, node_bootstrap_success, etcd_latency
Wire metrics to Console: dashboard, alert rules, and drilldowns
CI: add terraform e2e job that runs canary create/promote/rollback using short-lived test VPC
Documentation: Confluence design doc, runbook, and upgrade playbook
Security review and IAM policy audit
QA: chaos test to simulate API server failure and verify rollback path
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Transient double control-plane increases cost — Mitigation: allow configurable staging window and tagging for cost tracking
Risk: Terraform provider limitations prevent fully immutable resources — Mitigation: implement hybrid paths with explicit preflight smoke tests and orchestrated drain
Risk: Probe false positives trigger unnecessary rollbacks — Mitigation: use rolling window aggregation, require two consecutive windows to fail, and allow manual override
Risk: IAM misconfig leads to privilege escalation — Mitigation: require security_review_required and include least-privilege policies in module examples
